sources.entry: CodeBurn - Menu bar app that shows what your AI coding tools cost, by project, model and task, across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and 38 more.

Codeburn by iamtoruk - Breakdown of local spend down by project, model, git branch and task. Tracks plan quotas, and identifies token waste, including unused MCP servers, verbose CLAUDE.md, repeated file reads, and more.

summary.one_liner: CodeBurn is a local CLI, desktop app, menu bar/tray widget and MCP server that breaks down your AI coding tool spend by project, model, git branch and task by reading the session files already on your disk.
summary.what_it_does: It reads session files written by AI coding tools (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others, 42 integrations in total) and prices every token to show what was spent, broken into tables by tool, model, project, git branch and task category. The `codeburn optimize` command flags wasted tokens such as repeated file reads, unused MCP servers and an overly long CLAUDE.md, and can apply config fixes with backups and undo. Plan and quota tracking lets you compare spend against a subscription and read live five-hour and weekly limits, and `codeburn guard` can warn or stop Claude Code sessions at set dollar caps. It also offers a desktop app, a macOS menu bar and Windows tray view, a browser dashboard, and a local MCP server so an agent can query its own usage.
use_cases: track how much Claude Code or Codex spending goes to each project
find wasted tokens in AI coding sessions
see AI tool cost per git branch or pull request
compare models on cost and first-try success rate
monitor Claude Max or Pro subscription usage against limits
set spending caps for Claude Code sessions
how_to_run: claude mcp add codeburn -- npx -y codeburn mcp
notable: Reads local session files only; no account, and the CLI sends no telemetry
Covers 42 AI coding tools, auto-detected with no configuration
optimize --apply backs up files before changing them, and act undo reverts them
Guard installs Claude Code hooks that warn at $5 and stop at $15 by default
Dollar figures are API-equivalent estimates from measured token counts, not invoices
caveats: Requires Node.js 22.13+ for the CLI; the desktop app runs on macOS and Windows, with Linux limited to a GNOME Shell extension
Dollar costs are API-rate equivalents, not what a flat-fee subscription actually bills
Some tools record no token counts, so their figures are estimated from content length
Per-session detail disappears when the tool deletes its transcripts (e.g. Claude Code after 30 days), though daily totals are kept
keywords: how much did my ai coding cost
see where my claude spending goes
track ai tool costs across projects
